analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3 head) and a new benchmark-table row at head line 572 for a `--prompt-prep` CPU-only prompt-preparation benchmark. The row is outside the supplied head excerpt (lines 1-404), so I relied on the patch hunk (@@ -569,6 +569,7 @@). No code, config defaults, endpoints, key custody, attestation, cache or fan-helper behavior changes. The documented benchmark loads only the tokenizer, runs on CPU and prints JSON. It touches no coordinator WebSocket, no Secure Enclave or App Attest material, no consumer prompts (A-001) and no SSD prefix cache (T-041). The row mentions the prompt token cache with background comparisons off. This implies a prompt token cache exists, but the diff gives no storage, persistence or encryption details, so it is not evidence of new at-rest exposure. The base and head excerpts I reviewed (base lines 1349-1806, head lines 1-404) contain the unchanged cache, logout, report, fan and App Attest text. Nothing in them is altered by the PR. Remaining integration question: the real code in ProviderBenchmark/PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift and any prompt-token-cache implementation are not supplied, so a code-level review of those would need the corresponding source units. This doc-only change does not create a threat-model gap by itself.
